title: Kobalos_Malware_Investigation_a44
description: You are an incident responder tasked with investigating a potential Kobalos malware infection in your organization's network. Kobalos is a complex, multiplatform malware that targets high-performance computing (HPC) clusters and other high-profile systems. It grants remote access to the file system, provides the ability to spawn terminal sessions, and allows proxying connections to other Kobalos-infected servers. Your goal is to identify and mitigate the threat.
outcomes: Identify and investigate suspicious services and processes.
Determine persistence mechanisms used by malware.
Analyze network traffic for command-and-control (C2) communication.
Collect forensic evidence and contain the threat.

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content: You are an incident responder tasked with investigating a potential Kobalos malware infection in your organization's network. Kobalos is a complex, multiplatform malware that targets high-performance computing (HPC) clusters and other high-profile systems. It grants remote access to the file system, provides the ability to spawn terminal sessions, and allows proxying connections to other Kobalos-infected servers. Your goal is to identify and mitigate the threat.

levels.title: Get Access
levels.cloud_content: Access the target host via SSH using the following credentials: Username: cyrano, Password: cyrano.
levels.local_content: Access the target host via SSH using the following credentials: Username: cyrano, Password: cyrano.

levels.title: Suspicious Service Discovery
levels.content: While monitoring the network, you noticed unusual outbound connections from the `target` host. Investigate the host to identify any unauthorized or suspicious services running. The flag is a port number.
levels.solution: To identify suspicious services, use the command `netstat -tuln` to list all running services and their associated ports. Look for any services that seem out of place or unfamiliar, specifically the port 7070. The flag is the port number 7070.

hints.title: Conceptual Guidance
hints.content: Check the list of running services and look for any that seem out of place or unfamiliar.

hints.title: Command Suggestion
hints.content: Use the command `netstat -tuln` to list all running services and their associated ports.

hints.title: Near-Spoiler Hint
hints.content: Look for the port 7070 in the list of running services.

levels.title: Persistence Discovery
levels.content: You have identified a suspicious service running on the `target` host. Determine how this service is automatically started after a system reboot. The flag is a service name.
levels.solution: To identify persistence mechanisms, use the command `systemctl list-unit-files --type=service` to examine systemd services. Look for the service named `payload-transfer.service`. The flag is the service name payload-transfer.service.

hints.title: Conceptual Guidance
hints.content: Examine systemd services to find any related to the suspicious service.

hints.title: Command Suggestion
hints.content: Use the command `systemctl list-unit-files --type=service` to examine systemd services.

levels.title: C2 Communication Discovery (Port)
levels.content: The suspicious service on the `target` host appears to be communicating with an external command-and-control server. Determine which network port is used for this communication. The flag is a port number.
levels.solution: To identify the network port used for C2 communication, use the command `netstat -tuln` to list all network connections and listen ports. Look for the port 7070. The flag is the port number 7070.

hints.title: Conceptual Guidance
hints.content: Check the network connections and listen ports to find the one used by the suspicious service.

hints.title: Command Suggestion
hints.content: Use the command `netstat -tuln` to list all network connections and listen ports.

hints.title: Near-Spoiler Hint
hints.content: Look for the port 7070 in the list of network connections.
